newsitem.title: GERMANY: Continental says to cut German tyre output. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Continental says to cut German tyre output. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]

text.p: German tyre maker Continental AG said on Tuesday it would move nearly half of the domestic passenger vehicle tyre production at its Hanover factory outside Germany (corrects to add reference to moving production abroad).

Continental, which produces about 1.85 million passenger vehicle tyres annually in Germany, said it would move production of about 850,000 tyres to the Czech Republic and other countries during the rest of 1997.

Continental spokesman Dieter von Herz said the plan will require job cuts in Germany and employees working an additional 15 minutes without more pay to secure jobs and save about 35 million marks ($20 million) in costs at the production plant in Hanover.
The tyre maker's workforce at the plant will be cut to about 2,500 from the current level of 2,714, according to a pact that Continental reached with its works council.
But Continental said production of about 800,000 commercial vehicle tyres a year at the Hanover plant would not be affected by the pact.
